No fewer than 1.6 million artisanal miners under the National Artisanal and Small Scale Mining Cooperative Society have appealed for inclusion in the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. The miners who work in Nasarawa, Zamfara, Niger, Plateau, Kaduna, Taraba, Bauchi and other mineral-producing states noted that they work without modern equipment, protective clothing, technical training, affordable financing or access to legitimate mineral markets. Speaking on their behalf in a press statement made available to journalists in the Keffi Local Government Area of Nasarawa State on Sunday, the group’s National President, Abdullah Dantansidi, noted that such a situation exposes them to health risks, accidents and poverty, in spite of the mineral wealth in their communities. Dantansidi said, “Beneath our soil lie mineral resources capable of transforming our economy, creating jobs, and reducing our dependence on oil. Yet the men and women whose hands uncover this wealth are often among the poorest and most vulnerable Nigerians. “Across Nasarawa, Zamfara, Niger, Plateau, Kaduna, Taraba, Bauchi and other mineral-producing states, our miners go into pits daily with little more than hoes, shovels, and determination. They risk their health and their lives.” He, therefore, urged the President to include artisanal miners in the Renewed Hope Agenda through a dedicated empowerment and safety programme. Meanwhile, Dantansidi commended the Federal Government for its efforts to formalise artisanal mining through registered cooperatives, as he advocated that the ongoing reforms should reach ordinary miners in remote communities. According to him, about 1.6 million Nigerians are directly engaged in artisanal and small-scale mining, with millions of family members depending on the sector. We are asking for the practical support that will enable ordinary miners to comply with those regulations and earn a decent living. “Behind every mineral is a human being. A father struggling to provide for his family. A mother working to educate her children. A young Nigerian seeking an honest livelihood. “Let the Renewed Hope Agenda reach the mining pits, the rural communities and the hardworking Nigerians whose contributions often go unrecognised. “We do not ask for charity. We ask for opportunity, protection, recognition, and a fair chance to contribute to the greatness of our country. When you empower Nigeria’s 1.6 million artisanal miners, you improve millions of livelihoods, strengthen rural communities, and give real meaning to Renewed Hope.” Dantansidi appealed to Tinubu to establish a Renewed Hope Artisanal Miners Empowerment and Safety Programme, which should be built on existing initiatives of the Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development. He listed six priority areas for the programme, which include: recognition, registration and licensing; modern equipment and shared mining facilities; safety training and protection; affordable financing and cooperative development; fair mineral markets and local value addition; and community development and family welfare. He urged the President to direct the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, to engage representatives of artisanal mining cooperatives nationwide, and also proposed that the engagement should begin within 90 days. Dantansidi said the miners were ready to organise themselves, meet appropriate standards and work with government institutions. Collins Agwam
